articles.title: Subject matter
articles.requirement: Lays down rules on the institutional framework for AML/CFT, including FIUs, supervisors, beneficial ownership registers, risk assessment, and cooperation mechanisms.

articles.title: Definitions
articles.requirement: Defines key terms including obliged entities, beneficial owner, FIU, supervisory authority, high-risk third country, and other terms complementing the AMLR definitions.

articles.title: Identification of risk
articles.requirement: Member States must identify, assess, understand, and mitigate ML/TF risks affecting them, keeping the assessment up to date and making results available to obliged entities and supervisors.

articles.title: National risk assessment
articles.requirement: Member States must carry out a national risk assessment covering all ML/TF risks, including those related to legal persons, legal arrangements, non-profit organisations, and new products and technologies.

articles.title: Sector-specific risk assessment
articles.requirement: Supervisors must carry out risk assessments of the sectors and entities under their supervision, identifying sector-wide ML/TF risks and informing obliged entities of findings.

articles.title: Statistics on effectiveness
articles.requirement: Member States must maintain comprehensive statistics on AML/CFT effectiveness including STRs filed, investigations, prosecutions, convictions, assets frozen and confiscated, and supervision activities.

articles.title: Designation of AML/CFT supervisory authorities
articles.requirement: Member States must designate supervisory authorities responsible for monitoring obliged entities' compliance with AML/CFT requirements, with clear mandates and adequate powers.

articles.title: General supervisory powers
articles.requirement: AML/CFT supervisors must have powers to compel production of information, conduct on-site and off-site supervision, issue guidance, take enforcement action, and impose sanctions.

articles.title: Risk-based supervision
articles.requirement: Supervisors must adopt a risk-based approach to supervision, allocating resources proportionate to the ML/TF risks of obliged entities under their remit, with documented risk assessments.

articles.title: Supervisory activities and priorities
articles.requirement: Supervisors must establish annual supervisory plans, conduct regular and ad-hoc inspections, and review the adequacy of policies, procedures, and controls of obliged entities.

articles.title: Supervision of cross-border groups
articles.requirement: Home and host supervisors must cooperate on supervision of obliged entities operating cross-border, including through AML/CFT colleges where appropriate.

articles.title: Cooperation between AML/CFT supervisors and prudential supervisors
articles.requirement: AML/CFT supervisors and prudential supervisors must share information relevant to their respective tasks, including ML/TF risk findings and supervisory concerns.

articles.title: Self-regulatory bodies
articles.requirement: Where self-regulatory bodies supervise certain obliged entities (e.g., legal professionals), Member States must ensure they have adequate powers, resources, and are subject to public-authority oversight.

articles.title: Notification of criminal activity to FIU
articles.requirement: Supervisors must promptly inform the FIU when they discover facts that could be related to money laundering or terrorist financing during their supervisory activities.

articles.title: Establishment and status of FIUs
articles.requirement: Each Member State must establish a single FIU as a national centre for receiving, analysing, and disseminating STRs and other information relevant to ML/TF. FIUs must be operationally independent.

articles.title: Functions of FIUs
articles.requirement: FIUs must receive and analyse STRs and other reports from obliged entities, request additional information, disseminate results to law enforcement, and provide feedback to reporting entities.

articles.title: FIU access to information
articles.requirement: FIUs must have direct or indirect access to financial, administrative, and law enforcement information necessary for their functions, including BO registers and tax databases.

articles.title: FIU analysis function
articles.requirement: FIUs must conduct operational analysis (focused on individual cases) and strategic analysis (identifying ML/TF trends, patterns, and typologies) and disseminate results.

articles.title: FIU dissemination
articles.requirement: FIUs must disseminate the results of their analysis spontaneously or upon request to competent authorities, with appropriate protections for the confidentiality of the information.

articles.title: Suspension and non-execution of transactions
articles.requirement: FIUs must have the power to suspend or withhold consent to a transaction for a limited period to analyse, assess, and disseminate an STR where ML/TF is suspected.

articles.title: FIU feedback to obliged entities
articles.requirement: FIUs must provide timely and adequate feedback to obliged entities on the quality and usefulness of STRs filed, including typologies and sanitised case studies.

articles.title: Cooperation between FIUs
articles.requirement: FIUs must cooperate with each other, exchanging information spontaneously or upon request, using the FIU.net or successor secure communication system.

articles.title: Joint analysis by FIUs
articles.requirement: FIUs may conduct joint analyses of cross-border cases, supported by AMLA, with common dissemination rules and protections.

articles.title: Central BO registers — legal persons
articles.requirement: Member States must ensure corporate and other legal entities hold adequate, accurate, and current information on their beneficial owners and make this available to the central register.

articles.title: Information held in the central register — legal persons
articles.requirement: Central registers must contain the name, date of birth, nationality, country of residence, and nature and extent of beneficial interest of each beneficial owner of legal persons.

articles.title: Accuracy of BO information — legal persons
articles.requirement: Member States must ensure mechanisms to verify accuracy and currency of BO information, including discrepancy reporting by obliged entities and sanctions for non-compliance.

articles.title: BO registers — trusts and legal arrangements
articles.requirement: Member States must ensure trustees disclose their status and provide beneficial ownership information to the central register of the Member State in which the trust is administered.

articles.title: Access to BO registers
articles.requirement: BO information must be accessible to competent authorities, FIUs, and obliged entities performing CDD. Certain information must also be accessible to any person with a legitimate interest.

articles.title: Interconnection of BO registers
articles.requirement: Member States must ensure their central BO registers are interconnected via the BORIS system, enabling cross-border access to BO information by competent authorities.

articles.title: Bank account registers
articles.requirement: Member States must establish centralised bank account registries or electronic data retrieval systems enabling identification of bank account holders by FIUs and competent authorities.

articles.title: Real estate registers
articles.requirement: Member States must ensure competent authorities have access to information enabling identification of owners of real property, through registers or electronic data retrieval systems.

articles.title: AMLA coordination role
articles.requirement: AMLA supports and coordinates cooperation among national FIUs and supervisory authorities, develops technical standards, and mediates disagreements.

articles.title: AML/CFT colleges
articles.requirement: Lead supervisors must set up AML/CFT colleges for cross-border groups posing higher ML/TF risk, ensuring information exchange and coordinated supervisory activities.

articles.title: Administrative sanctions and measures
articles.requirement: Member States must ensure supervisory authorities can impose effective, proportionate, and dissuasive administrative sanctions and measures for AML/CFT breaches.

articles.title: Criminal penalties for ML/TF
articles.requirement: Member States must ensure that ML and TF are punishable by effective, proportionate, and dissuasive criminal penalties, including imprisonment of at least four years for serious offences.
